trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full-context read of rem:confinement-sdp-vs-lp (statement + one para). All ten categories judged; the block has no trap construction. THREE mathematical defects reported, each checked against the primal it cites (mass-theory/confinement-sdp.md gives min_{Phi >= 0} <T, Phi>): (i) 'the LP provides a lower bound on the SDP' is backwards - restricting Phi to the diagonal shrinks the feasible set of a MINIMISATION, so the LP optimum is >= the SDP optimum, an UPPER bound (the .ts tag 'lp-relaxation' has the same inversion: this is a restriction, not a relaxation); (ii) 'the rank-1 restriction Phi = diag(x)' misnames it - diag(x) has rank equal to its number of nonzero entries, so the restriction is diagonal, not rank-1; (iii) 'For most baryonic and light-nuclear configurations, the Wedderburn decomposition has 1-dimensional blocks' fails for the baryon case itself - H_3(q) has blocks of dimension 1, 2, 1, and the 2-dimensional (2,1) block is the physically load-bearing one (it is where the isospin singlet draws its entire weight under convention D, per prop:branching-identity-isospin-weights).
